literature_notes: All six ledger lines (L1–L6) describe the same experimental modality: full-length CDHR5-S and CDHR5-L expressed as C-terminally tagged EGFP-fusion proteins in LLC-PK1-CL4 cells. CDHR5 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein: the large ectodomain occupies residues 26–668 (extracellular), the TM spans 669–690, and the C-terminal tail occupies 691–845 (intracellular). A C-terminal EGFP fusion therefore sits on the INTRACELLULAR face and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. No ledger line mentions an N-terminal tag, an internal extracellular loop insertion, a FLAG/HA/Myc/ALFA/V5 tag, a HaloTag/SNAP-tag, a transposon screen, or any other modality that would ground an extracellular site. L5 explicitly flags that C-terminal tagging of CDHR5-L likely disrupts its PDZ-binding motif (PBM), and L6 reports that an untagged control was required to verify apical targeting. Because no ledger line supports an insertion on the extracellular face, sites = [].

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal EGFP fusion (after residue 845) is on the intracellular face; construct traffics correctly to the apical brush border but L5 notes it likely disrupts the PDZ-binding motif of the CDHR5-L isoform.

C-terminal EGFP tagging of CDHR5-L was assessed to likely disrupt PBM function because a canonical PDZ-binding motif requires a free C-terminal hydroxyl group; an untagged control (L6) was needed to confirm apical targeting was unaffected.
